summary: The paper addresses a genuine and practically relevant phenomenon—the PCC plateau in attention-based regression under joint MSE+PCC training—through two formal analyses: a gradient-ratio bottleneck (Corollary 2.1) and a PCC-gain capacity bound for convex aggregators (Theorem 2.2). The proposed ECA framework is directly motivated by these findings. However, statistical rigor is inadequate across most benchmarks (missing error bars, large variances that dwarf claimed gains, no significance tests), ablation coverage is limited to UCI tasks only, the related-work section is thin for the scope of claims, and several theoretical conditions are non-trivially restrictive without empirical validation of whether they hold in the tested settings.
strengths: The two-perspective decomposition (optimization dynamics vs. model capacity) is clean and well-motivated; the MSE–std–correlation decomposition (Proposition 2.1) and the convex-hull PCC gain bound (Theorem 2.2) are the most novel parts and provide principled grounding for ECA.

The ECA framework is a tight, theory-to-method correspondence: each of the three components (SRA, DATS, DNPL) maps directly to an identified bottleneck, with clear ablations confirming per-component contribution on UCI tasks.

The experimental scope is appropriately diverse—synthetic (controllable homogeneity), tabular (UCI), high-homogeneity real data (spatial transcriptomics), and multimodal time-series (MOSI)—and the spatial transcriptomics results (+14–16% PCC) are striking if they hold up statistically.

Corollary 2.2 explicitly links within-sample dispersion σ_s to PCC gradient magnitude, providing a formal handle on the homogeneity dependence that motivates DATS, and this is validated qualitatively on synthetic data.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical evidence is insufficient across most benchmarks. Table 2 (MOSI) reports single-run point estimates with no variance; Table 3 (spatial transcriptomics) shows standard deviations that are comparable to the gains themselves (e.g., PCC@F: 0.602±0.160 → 0.690±0.202, overlap is nearly complete at one standard deviation). No significance tests are reported anywhere. The Online News UCI improvement (PCC 0.408→0.420) is small enough to be within noise on a single run.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over at least 5 seeds for all datasets; include a paired t-test or Wilcoxon test for each benchmark; or widen the confidence intervals and qualify claims accordingly. For spatial transcriptomics, verify whether the three-fold variance is dominated by fold-level split variability or run-level noise.

key_concerns.issue: Ablation studies appear only for UCI tasks. For the two high-homogeneity benchmarks (spatial transcriptomics and MOSI) where the theory is most predictive, there are no component-wise ablations (SRA, DATS, DNPL individually). These are precisely the settings where the theory's claims should be most clearly confirmed.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add component ablations for at least the spatial transcriptomics dataset, which is the most compelling real-data result, and for MOSI. A table analogous to Table 1 for each setting would substantially strengthen the claims.

key_concerns.issue: Theorem 2.2 requires R < σ_0/‖w‖_2 for the bound to be finite; as R → σ_0/‖w‖_2 the bound diverges. The paper does not check whether this condition holds in any of the tested datasets, nor discuss what happens when it is violated. Without this check, the bound's applicability to the experiments is unclear.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report the empirical ratio R/(σ_0/‖w‖_2) for each dataset, confirm the condition is satisfied, and add a remark on what the framework implies when R is not small.

key_concerns.issue: Corollary 2.1 derives the gradient ratio bound under the assumption ρ ∈ [0,1], which excludes the common case of negative initial correlation. The paper does not discuss or validate this restriction, nor whether the O(1/σ_y^{3/2}) rate holds outside this range.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State the assumption prominently and provide a brief discussion (or supplementary proof sketch) of the behavior when ρ < 0. Show empirically that ρ stays non-negative throughout training in the experiments, or generalize the bound.

key_concerns.issue: Table 1 as extracted appears to have truncated rows for several ablation conditions—the numeric entries cut off mid-row for multiple ablation variants. It is unclear whether this is a text-extraction artifact or a formatting issue in the submission; either way, the ablation data in Table 1 is not fully readable and this must be resolved.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Ensure Table 1 is self-contained and all numeric cells are present and properly formatted in the final submission.

key_concerns.issue: The related-work section is too brief for the scope of the contribution. In particular, multi-task loss balancing (gradient surgery, loss weighting, PCGrad, GradNorm) is directly relevant to the MSE–PCC conflict but not discussed; and the literature on attention temperature scaling / entropy regularization is absent despite the close relation to DATS.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph comparing to gradient-balancing approaches in multi-task learning, and to prior adaptive-temperature softmax work, explaining how this work differs from both.

key_concerns.issue: Key hyperparameters of ECA (T_min, β, γ_max, λ_γ, λ_PCC) are mentioned but not ablated or reported as final values in the main paper. The MLP architecture for γ_s is described only as 'small' and 'sample-specific'.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (at minimum a 2×2 grid for the most sensitive parameters) and report final hyperparameter values in a reproducibility table in the main text or appendix.

questions_for_authors: Theorem 2.2 requires R < σ_0/‖w‖_2. What are the empirical values of this ratio across your datasets, and does the condition hold for spatial transcriptomics where σ is reported as 0.068?

The statistical variance in Table 3 is very large relative to the gains. Is the reported ± value across folds (split variance) or across seeds within each fold (run variance)? How many random seeds were used?
For MOSI (Table 2), only ALMT+ECA is shown; other baselines are not ablated with ECA. Is the improvement from ECA specific to ALMT, or does it generalize to other MSA models?

The analysis in the main paper is for a single-layer attention aggregation followed by a linear head. Section E (appendix) extends this to deep architectures—what are the key assumptions required for the bounds to transfer, and do they hold for multi-layer Transformers used in the UCI experiments?

DATS uses a sample-specific temperature inversely proportional to within-sample dispersion. How sensitive is ECA performance to the choice of T_min and β, and is there a principled way to set these without dataset-specific tuning?
calibration_check: The claims are partially well-scoped—the PCC plateau is framed as specific to attention-based regression with joint MSE+PCC training—but the spatial transcriptomics gains are presented as absolute percentage improvements ('+14.64%') without acknowledging that overlapping confidence intervals make statistical significance uncertain, and the 'first rigorous theoretical analysis' claim is strong given the thin related-work coverage of adjacent multi-task gradient-balancing literature.

significance.justification: The PCC plateau is a practically common failure mode in high-value application domains (pathology, sentiment analysis, spatial transcriptomics), and a principled mechanism plus plug-in fix would be widely citable if the experimental evidence were stronger.

novelty.justification: The formal capacity bound for convex aggregators (Theorem 2.2) and the gradient-ratio decay analysis (Corollary 2.1) are genuinely new; individual components of ECA (residual scaling, temperature adaptation, loss reweighting) are not novel in isolation but their theory-motivated combination is.

rigor.justification: The theoretical derivations appear correct given their stated assumptions, but the assumptions (ρ ≥ 0, R < σ_0/‖w‖_2) are non-trivially restrictive and not empirically validated; the depth generalization is deferred to the appendix without summary in the main text.

statistical_soundness.justification: No significance tests anywhere; MOSI and UCI results have no reported variance; spatial transcriptomics three-fold standard deviations span nearly the full magnitude of the reported gains, making the largest claimed improvements statistically ambiguous.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper is honest about the homogeneity-dependence caveat and acknowledges that improvements are task-dependent, but presents large percentage improvements without confidence intervals and claims 'first rigorous theoretical analysis' without adequately surveying gradient-balancing or adaptive-attention literature.

clarity.justification: The narrative from theory to method is clear and well-organized; however, notational overloading (σ_y for both prediction and ground-truth std), an apparently truncated Table 1, and inline figure captions in the extracted text reduce readability.

structure_compliance.justification: Follows standard ICLR structure (Abstract, Introduction, Theory, Method, Related Work, Experiments, Conclusion) with appropriate section depth; the related work section is notably short relative to the contribution scope.

reproducibility.justification: The MLP architecture for γ_s and several critical hyperparameters (T_min, β, γ_max, λ_γ) are not reported in the main text; data processing follows cited baselines, which partially mitigates the concern, but ECA-specific configuration details needed for reproduction are insufficient.

related_work.justification: The two-paragraph related work section omits directly relevant work on multi-task gradient balancing (GradNorm, PCGrad, loss weighting schemes) and adaptive-temperature attention, which are close prior art for the MSE-PCC conflict and DATS respectively.

figure_quality.justification: Captions indicate that Figure 5 (synthetic training curves by homogeneity level) and Figure 6 (per-fold PCC/MSE curves) directly support the core theoretical claims; Figure 3 validates Corollary 2.1 empirically; Table 1 is apparently truncated, which reduces the information value of the ablation presentation.

breadth_generality.justification: Four dataset types is reasonable scope, but ablation studies appear only for UCI tasks; no competing alternatives to ECA's individual components are evaluated; hyperparameter sensitivity is not studied; and the claim of generality beyond the tested architectures rests on an appendix argument not summarized in the main paper.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: the theoretical contribution is interesting and the problem is real, but the statistical validation is insufficient to support the empirical claims, ablations are incomplete across the most important benchmarks, and the related work and reproducibility gaps are non-trivial; resubmission after substantial revision is warranted.
